actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing Observation Shift Models
PROPOSAL: Experiment (1hr, 7 GPUs) - Train a set of baseline models (GPB, BCQ, CQL) on the Offline Robot Navigation dataset (Offline Robot Navigation v2) and a newer set of models specifically tailored to handle observation shifts (Shift-A2C, Shift-CQL, Shift-GEL). Evaluate these models on unseen episodes with unknown observation shifts and compare their performance on the Precision metric, which captures the ability of the agent to adapt to changing observation functions.
CONTROLS: Include ablations of each model type (e.g., train without the shift component), standard offline RL methods as baselines, and a comparison with online RL algorithms (e.g., SAC).
COST: 1 GPU-hour model interactions, 6 GPU-hours preprocessing, testing. Total: 7 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: The models specifically designed to handle observation shifts (Shift-A2C, Shift-CQL, Shift-GEL) are expected to outperform the standard offline RL models (GPB, BCQ, CQL) by a small margin, highlighting the challenge of handling observation shifts. The test may fail if the Shift models perform too similarly to the baseline models, indicating that the observation shift adaptation components are not effective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Offset Estimation Techniques
PROPOSAL: Experiment (3hr, 9 GPUs) - Design and evaluate methods for estimating the time-varying offsets in the observation function, using the Offline Robot Manipulation dataset (D4RL's robotic table setting). Consider the following techniques: (1) offline learning of an offset predictor, (2) incremental learning of an offset predictor, (3) online learning of an offset predictor (with synthetic shifts at test time), and (4) aligning the observations with a pre-estimated offset distribution. Evaluate each method's ability to recover the true offsets and its impact on downstream control performance.
CONTROLS: Include a comparison with existing methods for learning from stationary observation functions (e.g., GPB, CQL) and online learning methods (e.g., SAC), as well as experiments with different offset estimation intervals and histories.
COST: 3 CPU-years model interactions, 6 GPU-years preprocessing, testing. Total: 9 GPU-years.
PREDICTION: We expect that techniques (1) and (2) will be more effective than (3) and (4), as they are based on offline training and can capture global patterns in the offsets. This may fail if the dynamics of the robot environment are too complex, and the offset estimation techniques struggle to keep pace with the changing observation functions.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Offset Estimation Techniques
PROPOSAL: REVISED - Instead of evaluating all four techniques, we will retain (1) offline learning of an offset predictor and (2) incremental learning of an offset predictor. Additionally, we will compare these methods with a naive baseline that uses a constant offset estimate for each dimension (which could be an arbitrary pre-defined value). We will also modify the (1) and (2) to use self-supervised learning objectives to learn the offset predictors from the offline data, rather than using a separate loss function.
CONTROLS: Include a comparison with existing methods for learning from stationary observation functions (e.g., GPB, CQL) and online learning methods (e.g., SAC), as well as experiments with different offset estimation intervals and histories.
COST: 2 CPU-years model interactions, 4 GPU-years preprocessing, testing. Total: 6 GPU-years.
PREDICTION: We expect that the offline learning and incremental learning methods will perform significantly better than the naive baseline, since they adapt to the changing observation functions. We also expect (1) offline learning to perform slightly better than (2) incremental learning due to the greater availability of data for pre-training.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Offset Estimation Techniques

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Reinforcement Learning with Visual Feedback for Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will train a pre-existing multimodal large language model (MM-LM) with reinforcement learning, customizing the reward function to positively reinforce the production of coherent visual state transitions and discourage incoherent reasoning flows, using the visual feedback from output images.
CONTROLS: We will use a control group that receives standard reinforcement learning rewards, ignoring the visual aspects of generated images, as well as ablations that disable visual feedback or modify the customized reward function to test its sensitivity.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model trained with visual reinforcement learning should perform better than the control group, particularly on tasks requiring long compositional reasoning chains, but may struggle with instabilities in training, especially on more complex tasks such as jigsaw-solving.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Generation of Visual State Transitions using Similarity-based Attention Mechanisms
PROPOSAL: We will modify the existing MM-LM architecture to include a novel similarity-based attention mechanism that groups visually similar tokens together, reducing the quadratic cost of autoregressive generation and minimizing the need for Frederically updating the visual state, using a dataset specifically designed for test of efficiency.
CONTROLS: We will compare our modified model with a baseline version of the MM-LM that uses standard attention mechanisms, and also study the impact of scaling up the model size on the efficiency of visual state transitions.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The modified model should demonstrate faster and more efficient generation of visual state transitions, with a linear reduction in computational cost as the sequence length increases. However, it remains unclear how the similarity-based attention mechanism will affect the model's ability to reason over visually dissimilar scenes or objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditioning Visual Reasoning on High-Level Scene Structure via Top-Down Graph Attention
PROPOSAL: We will integrate a graph attention network (GAT) into the MM-LM to condition visual reasoning on high-level scene structure, enabling the model to better represent and reason about visual state transitions at a more abstract level, and use top-down graph attention to focus on relevant scene objects and spatial relationships.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model with a baseline version that uses standard attention mechanisms, and also study the impact of the GAT's graph structure on the model's reasoning capabilities.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model with top-down graph attention should improve the coherence and abstraction of visual state transitions, and enhance the model's ability to reason over complex scenes with multiple objects and spatial constraints. However, it may require more computational resources due to the added complexity of the graph attention network.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Reinforcement Learning with Visual Feedback for Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL: To better understand the impact of visual feedback on reinforcement learning, we will also study the effect of varying the frequency and type of visual rewards, using a more nuanced reward shaping scheme that encodes different levels of visual coherence and logic, and use a larger and more diverse set of tasks that require long compositional reasoning chains, as well as those that emphasize visual reasoning over text-based logic.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model trained with visual rewards to the original control group and ablations that disable visual feedback or modify the reward function, and also study the sensitivity of the model to different hyperparameters and training conditions.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model trained with the nuanced reward shaping scheme should exhibit improved performance on tasks that require long compositional reasoning chains and emphasize visual reasoning, particularly when combined with the efficient generation of visual state transitions and top-down graph attention mechanisms.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating the Efficacy of Reinforcement Learning with Visual Feedback for Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL (number 1): To better understand the impact of visual feedback on reinforcement learning, we will also study the effect of varying the frequency and type of visual rewards, using a more nuanced reward shaping scheme that encodes different levels of visual coherence and logic, and use a larger and more diverse set of tasks that require long compositional reasoning chains, as well as those that emphasize visual reasoning over text-based logic.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model trained with visual rewards to the original control group and ablations that disable visual feedback or modify the reward function, and also study the sensitivity of the model to different hyperparameters and training conditions.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model trained with the nuanced reward shaping scheme should exhibit improved performance on tasks that require long compositional reasoning chains and emphasize visual reasoning, particularly when combined with the efficient generation of visual state transitions and top-down graph attention mechanisms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Adversarial Visual Perturbations
PROPOSAL: We will test the robustness of the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning model to adversarial visual perturbations by adding noise or modifying the visual input in a way that requires the model to reason more efficiently or accurately, and compare the performance of the model to state-of-the-art attackers and defenses on a range of visual reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: We will use a range of baseline models and techniques for image generation and perturbation, as well as compare our model's performance on different types and levels of adversarial perturbation.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model should exhibit robustness to moderate levels of adversarial perturbation, but may struggle with more severe or sophisticated attacks, particularly those that target the model's specific vulnerabilities to visual reasoning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Visual Reasoning in Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Domain-Specific Knowledge Graphs
PROPOSAL: We will incorporate domain-specific knowledge graphs into the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning model to provide additional information about visual objects and their relationships, and evaluate the performance of the model on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning and domain-specific knowledge.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model with and without the knowledge graphs, and also study the impact of different knowledge graph structures and update mechanisms on the model's performance.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model with domain-specific knowledge graphs should exhibit improved performance on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning and domain-specific knowledge, but may require more computational resources and training data to effectively utilize the knowledge graphs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compositional Reasoning over Multiple Modalities with Hierarchical Attention and Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a hierarchical attention and reasoning mechanism that composes multiple visual reasoning tasks and leverages the semantic relationships between them to improve overall performance on complex multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model with and without hierarchical attention and reasoning, and also study the impact of different hierarchical structures and attention mechanisms on the model's performance.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model with hierarchical attention and reasoning should exhibit improved performance on complex multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks, but may require more computational resources and training data to effectively compose multiple visual reasoning tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Visual and Textual Representations on Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of different visual and textual representations on the performance of multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning models, including the effects of different image encoding techniques, text embedding methods, and visual-language fusion strategies.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model with different visual and textual representations, and also study the impact of combining different visual and textual representations on the model's performance.
COST: 280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model's performance may be sensitive to the choice of visual and textual representations, with some methods exhibiting better performance than others, particularly on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning or complex language understanding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study of Interleaved Textual and Visual Reasoning within Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive ablation study to investigate the importance of interleaved textual and visual reasoning for multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks, by comparing the performance of the model with different levels of interleaving and ablations of individual components.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the model with and without interleaved textual and visual reasoning, and also study the impact of different interleaving techniques, such as sequential or parallel reasoning, on the model's performance.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results of the ablation study should provide valuable insights into the relative importance of textual and visual reasoning within the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning framework, and help to identify key components that are essential for effective performance on multi-modal tasks.

propositions.texte: We will modify the existing MM-LM architecture to include a novel similarity-based attention mechanism that groups visually similar tokens together, reducing the quadratic cost of autoregressive generation and minimizing the need for Frederically updating the visual state, using a dataset specifically designed for test of efficiency.
propositions.titre: Efficient Generation of Visual State Transitions using Similarity-based Attention Mechanisms

propositions.controles: We will compare our model with a baseline version that uses standard attention mechanisms, and also study the impact of the GAT's graph structure on the model's reasoning capabilities.
propositions.prediction: The model with top-down graph attention should improve the coherence and abstraction of visual state transitions, and enhance the model's ability to reason over complex scenes with multiple objects and spatial constraints. However, it may require more computational resources due to the added complexity of the graph attention network.
propositions.texte: We will integrate a graph attention network (GAT) into the MM-LM to condition visual reasoning on high-level scene structure, enabling the model to better represent and reason about visual state transitions at a more abstract level, and use top-down graph attention to focus on relevant scene objects and spatial relationships.
propositions.titre: Conditioning Visual Reasoning on High-Level Scene Structure via Top-Down Graph Attention

propositions.controles: We will use a range of baseline models and techniques for image generation and perturbation, as well as compare our model's performance on different types and levels of adversarial perturbation.
propositions.prediction: The model should exhibit robustness to moderate levels of adversarial perturbation, but may struggle with more severe or sophisticated attacks, particularly those that target the model's specific vulnerabilities to visual reasoning.
propositions.texte: We will test the robustness of the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning model to adversarial visual perturbations by adding noise or modifying the visual input in a way that requires the model to reason more efficiently or accurately, and compare the performance of the model to state-of-the-art attackers and defenses on a range of visual reasoning tasks.
propositions.titre: Evaluating the Robustness of Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Adversarial Visual Perturbations

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the model with and without the knowledge graphs, and also study the impact of different knowledge graph structures and update mechanisms on the model's performance.
propositions.prediction: The model with domain-specific knowledge graphs should exhibit improved performance on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning and domain-specific knowledge, but may require more computational resources and training data to effectively utilize the knowledge graphs.
propositions.texte: We will incorporate domain-specific knowledge graphs into the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning model to provide additional information about visual objects and their relationships, and evaluate the performance of the model on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning and domain-specific knowledge.
propositions.titre: Improving Visual Reasoning in Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Domain-Specific Knowledge Graphs

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the model with and without hierarchical attention and reasoning, and also study the impact of different hierarchical structures and attention mechanisms on the model's performance.
propositions.prediction: The model with hierarchical attention and reasoning should exhibit improved performance on complex multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks, but may require more computational resources and training data to effectively compose multiple visual reasoning tasks.
propositions.texte: We will introduce a hierarchical attention and reasoning mechanism that composes multiple visual reasoning tasks and leverages the semantic relationships between them to improve overall performance on complex multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks.
propositions.titre: Compositional Reasoning over Multiple Modalities with Hierarchical Attention and Reasoning

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the model with different visual and textual representations, and also study the impact of combining different visual and textual representations on the model's performance.
propositions.prediction: The model's performance may be sensitive to the choice of visual and textual representations, with some methods exhibiting better performance than others, particularly on tasks that require high-level visual reasoning or complex language understanding.
propositions.texte: We will investigate the impact of different visual and textual representations on the performance of multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning models, including the effects of different image encoding techniques, text embedding methods, and visual-language fusion strategies.
propositions.titre: Analyzing the Impact of Visual and Textual Representations on Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

propositions.controles: We will compare the performance of the model with and without interleaved textual and visual reasoning, and also study the impact of different interleaving techniques, such as sequential or parallel reasoning, on the model's performance.
propositions.prediction: The results of the ablation study should provide valuable insights into the relative importance of textual and visual reasoning within the multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning framework, and help to identify key components that are essential for effective performance on multi-modal tasks.
propositions.texte: We will conduct a comprehensive ablation study to investigate the importance of interleaved textual and visual reasoning for multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning tasks, by comparing the performance of the model with different levels of interleaving and ablations of individual components.
propositions.titre: Ablation Study of Interleaved Textual and Visual Reasoning within Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integrated Cross-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Controlled Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Investigate a multi-modal transformer architecture where text and image generation are tightly integrated within a single step, matching and conditioning each other. This is achieved by using a novel token-level cross attention mechanism that weights the contribution of text and visual tokens to the final output, and controls the image generation by a series of well-defined visual operations (e.g. cropping, drawing) crafted as specific discrete text tokens. This architecture is then optimized using a custom variant of the mixed beam search algorithm that tunes the visual and text components separately, encouraging coherent visual and text-based reasoning flows.
CONTROLS: Compare against MLLMs optimized with reinforcement learning, state-of-the-art GAN-based visual understanding models, and standard autoregressive image generation architectures.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This architecture should lead to performance gains on reasoning-intensive tasks that require coherent text-image flows, with particular improvement on tasks like visual question answering. However, we expect potential failure in handling visually complex tasks requiring highly detailed or novel image transformations due to the limited scope of the controlled visual operations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Ray-Casting for Long-range Visual Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Develop a custom visual reasoning component that, in conjunction with the text generation component from the integrated architecture of proposal 1, can robustly handle long-range visual reasoning tasks by explicitly encoding scene geometry and object interactions. This is achieved through a learned ray-casting module that generates a (differential) visibility map for each scene, allowing the model to reason about occlusion, containment, and adjacency relationships between objects in 3D space. This learned component is trained using a combination of 3D scene understanding and collision-based distances as proxy objectives, along with reinforcement learning for evaluation.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against human-made level design evaluations and against the standard visual reasoning metrics (SPC and SPQR) on vis-doom and AI2-thor tasks.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This proposal should significantly help the integrated architecture from proposal 1 in tasks requiring reasoning about 3D spaces and occlusions. We expect minor complications with significant simplifications or artifacts in scene rendering.

This module is designed to dynamically prioritize areas of a scene that require detailed analysis for accurate reasoning, reducing traversal complexity and potential ambiguities in collision detection and occlusion analysis. Include the refinement of training objectives with extensive ray-tracing simulation data (Volassis caches, Synthetic VTT, older few-shot & transit simulations).

TITLE: Bayesian Self-Modifying Weights for Adaptable Visual Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Develop a technique that enables the Integrated Cross-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Controlled Image Generation to learn an adaptation of the module's weights as a function of task-specific uncertainty during inference. This is achieved by incorporating a probabilistic layer that updates the model's weights in a manner that strongly emphasizes regions of low task uncertainty. The self-modifying weights are learned through a meta-learning process during pretraining on Bayesian uncertainty metric (e.g., estimated posterior mean and variance). We expect the incorporation of Bayesian assumptions to yield improvements in model generalization on visually grounded training tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Robust Ray-Casting for Long-range Visual Reasoning
PROPOSAL: To improve the robustness and generalizability of the enhanced ray-casting component from proposal 2, integrate a contrastive learning framework that encourages the model to distinguish its own rendering of a scene from synthetic or realistic alternatives. This contrastive loss enables the model to identify key visual features and geometric structures that are essential for robust reasoning, and to detect and compensate for potential artifacts or bias. Combine this with the existing component to form a hybrid approach that offers improved performance on visually complex tasks such as 3D reconstruction and scene understanding.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art visual reasoning models, including those that use ray-casting and contrastive learning, on a suite of challenging scene understanding and 3D reconstruction benchmarks.
COST: 6,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hybrid approach should demonstrate significant improvements in robustness and generalizability, with potential failures in tasks that require highly detailed or nuanced geometric understanding, such as reconstructing scenes with complex topological features.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual-Spatial Working Memory Extension for Multi-Modal Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Develop an extension to the Integrated Cross-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Controlled Image Generation that incorporates a visual-spatial working memory mechanism. This mechanism allows the model to maintain and manipulate a temporary, mental representation of the visual scene, enabling it to reason about spatial relationships and maintain context over multiple reasoning steps. Inspired by cognitive architectures such as SOAR, the mechanism will utilize neural networks to build and maintain a dynamic, episodic memory. This extension aims to improve performance on visually grounded tasks that require sustained attention and working memory, such as following instructions or reasoning about complex scenes.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against benchmarks that require spatial reasoning, such as the spatial reasoning portion of the bAbI tasks and the Blocksworld environment.
COST: 9,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The visual-spatial working memory extension should lead to significant improvements on tasks that require complex spatial reasoning and context maintenance. However, we expect to see performance degradation on tasks with short reasoning times or focused queries, where the model may not have sufficient opportunity to utilize the working memory mechanism.

TITLE: Hierarchical Evaluation for Multi-Modal Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical evaluation framework that allows for the evaluation of multi-modal models on a variety of tasks and abstract levels. This framework combines task-specific evaluation metrics with a generalizable, level-based evaluation system that assesses the model's ability to reason at different levels of abstraction, from basic visual objects to more complex spatial relationships and abstract concepts. propositions.controles: Evaluate against benchmarks that require spatial reasoning, such as the spatial reasoning portion of the bAbI tasks and the Blocksworld environment.
propositions.prediction: The visual-spatial working memory extension should lead to significant improvements on tasks that require complex spatial reasoning and context maintenance. However, we expect to see performance degradation on tasks with short reasoning times or focused queries, where the model may not have sufficient opportunity to utilize the working memory mechanism.
propositions.texte: Develop an extension to the Integrated Cross-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Controlled Image Generation that incorporates a visual-spatial working memory mechanism. This mechanism allows the model to maintain and manipulate a temporary, mental representation of the visual scene, enabling it to reason about spatial relationships and maintain context over multiple reasoning steps. Inspired by cognitive architectures such as SOAR, the mechanism will utilize neural networks to build and maintain a dynamic, episodic memory. This extension aims to improve performance on visually grounded tasks that require sustained attention and working memory, such as following instructions or reasoning about complex scenes.
propositions.titre: Visual-Spatial Working Memory Extension for Multi-Modal Reasoning

propositions.controles: Evaluate against state-of-the-art multi-modal models on a range of tasks, including visual reasoning, language understanding, and multi-modal fusion.
propositions.prediction: The hierarchical evaluation framework should enable the models to demonstrate improved generalizability and abstraction capabilities, allowing them to navigate complex tasks and abstract level reasoning. However, we expect potential failures in cases where the abstract levels are too complex or the task-specific evaluation metrics are not aligned with the level-agnostic objectives.
propositions.texte: Develop a hierarchical evaluation framework that allows for the evaluation of multi-modal models on a variety of tasks and abstract levels. This framework combines task-specific evaluation metrics with a generalizable, level-based evaluation system that assesses the model's ability to reason at different levels of abstraction, from basic visual objects to more complex spatial relationships and abstract concepts. The framework will be trained on a combination of task-specific and level-agnostic evaluation objectives, allowing the model to generalize to new tasks and levels of abstraction.
propositions.titre: Hierarchical Evaluation for Multi-Modal Reasoning

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Efficient Sequence Modeling
PROPOSAL: We propose to leverage the capabilities of the Transformer-XL model, which is designed to handle long-range dependencies in sequencing tasks. We will extend this architecture to our multi-modal CoT model, allowing it to parallelize the processing of both textual and visual information across different time steps. This will enable the model to efficiently process long reasoning chains and mitigate the computational burden of our proposed unified multi-modal framework.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model to the standard transformer architecture, which requires sequential processing of image and text tokens, as well as to models that rely solely on programmatic visual operations.
COST: Estimated 5000 GPU-hours for training on a mix of synthetic and real-world data.
PREDICTION: Expected to outperform current state-of-the-art multi-modal CoT models on reasoning-intensive tasks by at least 10% due to improved efficiency. Potential performance improvement may be limited on tasks with large image outputs due to its specific implementation, possibly failing on these edge cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Attention Mechanisms for Multi-Modal CoT Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of attention mechanisms on the performance and stability of our proposed model. Specifically, we will explore the use of different attention variants, such as cross-attention, self-attention, and multi-head attention, to see if they can better capture the relationships between textual and visual information. Additionally, we will explore the use of attention as a mechanism to reduce the computational cost of processing long reasoning chains.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our results using the ablations of different attention mechanisms, and compare them to state-of-the-art models on tasks such as reasoning-driven text-to-image generation and visual question answering.
COST: Estimated 2000 GPU-hours for large-scale experiments on real-world data.
PREDICTION: Expected to find that the combination of multi-head attention and self-attention can lead to the best performance on multi-modal CoT tasks. This might fail if the capacity of our attention module is not sufficient to represent the complex relationships between textual and visual information in certain tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual-Textual Interaction Patterns in Multi-Modal CoT Reasoning
PROPOSAL: We will delve into the behavior of our proposed model and investigate the interaction patterns between textual and visual information during CoT reasoning. By analyzing the attention patterns and intermediate representations, we will identify the key features that both facilitate and hinder the convergence of our model. This analysis will inform the development of more effective architectures and training strategies for multi-modal CoT models.
CONTROLS: We will compare our model to existing multi-modal CoT models, and evaluate the fidelity of our analysis through large-scale visualizations and qualitative case studies on reasoning-intensive tasks.
COST: Estimated 1000 GPU-hours for data preprocessing and analysis.
PREDICTION: Expected to uncover novel insights into the interaction patterns between textual and visual information, which will facilitate the development of more effective models. However, the complexity of our model might make it challenging to interpret the results accurately, potentially failing to provide actionable insights into the model's behavior.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantifying the Gap in Egocentric Video Understanding
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of a strong egocentric video question answering (Q&A) baseline model on the existing egocentric video benchmarks (e.g., EPIC-100, Large-Scale Egocentric, and Interaction-aware) with and without eye-tracking gaze data, to quantify the gap in understanding user intent without gaze information.
CONTROLS: Compare the model's performance on EPIC-100 with and without gaze information, using metrics such as accuracy, and response time; baseline model: ViLT-B32, a pre-trained multimodal language model.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show a significant performance drop when removing gaze information, indicating the model's reliance on gaze cues to understand user intent; potential failure: over-reliance on gaze data in EPIC-100, limiting generalizability to other benchmarks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction
PROPOSAL: Modify the baseline model's visual token construction mechanism to incorporate eye-tracking gaze data, and evaluate its impact on egocentric video understanding.
CONTROLS: Compare the modified model's performance to the original baseline model on the egocentric video benchmarks with and without gaze information; use gaze data to guide token construction, focusing on gaze regions, gaze-attribution, visual-semantic alignment and object grounding; baseline model variant: ViLT-B32-Gaze, a modified version of ViLT-B32.
COST: 15 GPU-hours (5 hours per variant)
PREDICTION: Expected results show improved model performance when incorporating gaze-guided visual tokens, indicating the benefits of attending to user gaze cues; potential failure: over-integration of gaze data, leading to model over-reliance or decreased generalization to other tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Clarifying the Benefits of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous proposal by evaluating the benefits of gaze-guided visual token construction on variant tasks, such as action recognition, object grounding, and user intent prediction, to better understand its generalizability and the range of its advantages.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of ViLT-B32-Gaze on multiple tasks within the egocentric video benchmarks; validate the importance of gaze-guided visual token construction for different task distributions and regional attention patterns; use ablations of gaze attention and normalization techniques to isolate its benefits.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (up from original 5 hours, to accommodate the expanded evaluation)
PREDICTION: Expected results reinforce the benefits of gaze-guided visual token construction for user intent prediction and tasks requiring local attention to egocentric visual cues; potential failure: discovering benefits that are either too task-specific or confined to a narrow regime.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness Evaluation of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of ViLT-B32-Gaze to imperfect and inaccurate eye-tracking gaze data, simulating scenarios with noise, occlusions, or missing gaze information.
CONTROLS: Evaluate ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance on noisy and synthetic gaze data; compare to a gaze-free baseline model; and, assess its resilience to dataset-specific noise distributions, gaze sequences, and regional gaze patterns; use various metrics such as accuracy and attention alignment.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that ViLT-B32-Gaze adapts relatively well to imperfect or incomplete gaze data but can degrade under extreme noise scenarios; potential failure: discovering that the model's reliance on gaze data makes it sensitive to very minor noise levels, restricting its practical applications.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Grounded Evaluation of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction Robustness
PROPOSAL: Refine the robustness evaluation by grounding the assessment of ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance to scenario-specific gaze patterns and noise distributions, and comparing against a scenario-agnostic baseline.
CONTROLS: Compare ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance across multiple scenarios, such as object-centered vs. task-centered gaze, with varying levels of noise; evaluate its performance on a specific set of challenging scenarios; validate that robustness is scenario-dependent, rather than mere model parameter tuning; validate model robustness under anisotropic noise.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (increased from 20, to account for more comprehensive scenario analysis)
PREDICTION: Expected results indicate ViLT-B32-Gaze's ability to adapt to a variety of challenging scenarios while maintaining reliable performance in key case studies; potential failure: discovering that the model struggles on task-specific or high-noise scenarios, revealing existing vulnerabilities in the proposed method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Multi-Modal Fusion for Egocentric User Intent Understanding
PROPOSAL: Integrate multimodal fusion capabilities into ViLT-B32-Gaze, enabling it to leverage additional modalities like speech, keyboard input, or action recognition, to better understand user intent.
CONTROLS: Compare ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance on joint multimodal tasks to that on single-modal tasks (visual and gaze-based) using various fusion strategies (late fusion, early fusion, encoder-decoder fusion) and fusion modalities (voice, text, action); evaluate the impact of different fusion weights and modal combinations on user intent prediction.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show significant performance improvements from integrating additional modalities and careful fusion strategies in understanding user intent; potential failure: discovering that adding modalities leads to model overfitting, albeit larger capacity leading to device limiting computations.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Exploring the Effects of Modality Hierarchies and Fusion on Egocentric User Intent Understanding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effects of modality hierarchies (e.g., prioritizing gaze, speech, or action recognition) and fusion strategies (e.g., weighted or attention-based fusion) on ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance in understanding user intent.
CONTROLS: Compare the impact of modality hierarchies and fusion strategies on ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance using metrics such as accuracy, AUPRC, and Overall F1 Score; evaluate the trade-offs between modality hierarchy and fusion strategy; validate which fusion strategy and modality hierarchy results in better user intent understanding across multiple scenario types, tasks and hyperparameters.
COST: 35 GPU-hours (increased from 30, to account for more detailed exploration of fusion and modality hierarchies)
PREDICTION: Expected results provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationships between modality hierarchies, fusion strategies, and user intent understanding; reveal insights for tailoring ViLT-B32-Gaze to specific applications, devices and user interfaces; potential failure: discovering deficiencies in model generalizability and overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction and Multi-Modal Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze the benefits and limitations of gaze-guided visual token construction and multi-modal fusion in egocentric user intent understanding.
CONTROLS: Establish mathematical bounds on the benefits of gaze-guided visual token construction and multi-modal fusion; derive worst-case and average-case performance guarantees; analyze the effects of modality hierarchies and fusion strategies on model performance; use information-theoretic measures to quantify the importance of gaze and other modalities for user intent understanding.
COST: negligible, as this proposal focuses on theoretical work
PREDICTION: Expected results provide a solid theoretical foundation for further research on model architectures and fusion strategies; reveal which design choices lead to optimal performance in different scenarios; potential failure: discovering that the theoretical bounds are too loose or too tight, limiting their practical applicability.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Real-World Variability on Egocentric User Intent Understanding
PROPOSAL: Extend the exploration of ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance to more realistic scenarios, incorporating real-world variability in gaze data, camera motion, and environmental conditions; evaluate the model's ability to adapt to diverse environments and user behaviors.
CONTROLS: Adapt the real-world evaluation to various scenarios, such as different lighting conditions, screen sizes, or gaze intensity levels; simulate real-world variability in gaze data using techniques such as gaze-sampling or gaze-synthetic generation; validate that the model's adaptation capacity is linked to the quality of the fusion mechanism.
COST: 40 GPU-hours ( adds the cost for the real-world simulation)
PREDICTION: Expected results demonstrate ViLT-B32-Gaze's robustness in real-world scenarios, and the benefits and limitations of the fusion strategy under real-world conditions;  a concentration on the hardware, software or platform may prove effective or countering that appear when analyzing results simply.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Long-Term Effectiveness of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction in Egocentric User Intent Understanding
PROPOSAL: Conduct a long-term study to assess ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance on egocentric user intent understanding over a prolonged period of training and fine-tuning; monitor the model's adaptability to changing user behaviors, environmental conditions, and new task distributions.
CONTROLS: Set up a continuous training and evaluation framework for ViLT-B32-Gaze, utilizing active learning or streaming data to introduce new and challenging examples; evaluate the model's ability to generalize to unseen tasks, users, or environments; compare long-term performance with a gaze-free baseline model.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (significantly increased over previous proposals)
PREDICTION: Expected results provide insights into ViLT-B32-Gaze's long-term adaptability and effectiveness; demonstrate its ability to learn from and adapt to changing user behaviors and task distributions.

PROPOSAL 1: Quantifying the Gap in Egocentric Video Understanding
Evaluate the performance of a strong egocentric video question answering (Q&A) baseline model on the existing egocentric video benchmarks (e.g., EPIC-100, Large-Scale Egocentric, and Interaction-aware) with and without eye-tracking gaze data, to quantify the gap in understanding user intent without gaze information.
Controls: Compare the model's performance on EPIC-100 with and without gaze information, using metrics such as accuracy, and response time; baseline model: ViLT-B32, a pre-trained multimodal language model.
Estimated cost: 10 GPU-hours
Prediction: Expected results show a significant performance drop when removing gaze information, indicating the model's reliance on gaze cues to understand user intent; potential failure: over-reliance on gaze data in EPIC-100, limiting generalizability to other benchmarks.

PROPOSAL 2: Clarifying the Benefits of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction
Refine the previous proposal by evaluating the benefits of gaze-guided visual token construction on variant tasks, such as action recognition, object grounding, and user intent prediction, to better understand its generalizability and the range of its advantages.
Controls: Compare the performance of ViLT-B32-Gaze on multiple tasks within the egocentric video benchmarks; validate the importance of gaze-guided visual token construction for different task distributions and regional attention patterns; use ablations of gaze attention and normalization techniques to isolate its benefits.
Estimated cost: 10 GPU-hours (up from original 5 hours, to accommodate the expanded evaluation)
Prediction: Expected results reinforce the benefits of gaze-guided visual token construction for user intent prediction and tasks requiring local attention to egocentric visual cues; potential failure: discovering benefits that are either too task-specific or confined to a narrow regime.

PROPOSAL 3: Grounded Evaluation of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction Robustness
Refine the robustness evaluation by grounding the assessment of ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance to scenario-specific gaze patterns and noise distributions, and comparing against a scenario-agnostic baseline.
Controls: Compare ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance across multiple scenarios, such as object-centered vs. task-centered gaze, with varying levels of noise; evaluate its performance on a specific set of challenging scenarios; validate that robustness is scenario-dependent, rather than mere model parameter tuning; validate model robustness under anisotropic noise.
Estimated cost: 25 GPU-hours (increased from 20, to account for more comprehensive scenario analysis)
Prediction: Expected results indicate ViLT-B32-Gaze's ability to adapt to a variety of challenging scenarios while maintaining reliable performance in key case studies; potential failure: discovering that the model struggles on task-specific or high-noise scenarios, revealing existing vulnerabilities in the proposed method.

PROPOSAL 4: Exploring the Effects of Modality Hierarchies and Fusion on Egocentric User Intent Understanding
Investigate the effects of modality hierarchies (e.g., prioritizing gaze, speech, or action recognition) and fusion strategies (e.g., weighted or attention-based fusion) on ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance in understanding user intent.
Controls: Compare the impact of modality hierarchies and fusion strategies on ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance using metrics such as accuracy, AUPRC, and Overall F1 Score; evaluate the trade-offs between modality hierarchy and fusion strategy; validate which fusion strategy and modality hierarchy results in better user intent understanding across multiple scenario types, tasks and hyperparameters.
Estimated cost: 35 GPU-hours (increased from 30, to account for more detailed exploration of fusion and modality hierarchies)
Prediction: Expected results provide a comprehensive understanding of the relationships between modality hierarchies, fusion strategies, and user intent understanding; reveal insights for tailoring ViLT-B32-Gaze to specific applications, devices and user interfaces; potential failure: discovering deficiencies in model generalizability and overfitting.

PROPOSAL 5: Investigating the Impact of Real-World Variability on Egocentric User Intent Understanding
Extend the exploration of ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance to more realistic scenarios, incorporating real-world variability in gaze data, camera motion, and environmental conditions; evaluate the model's ability to adapt to diverse environments and user behaviors.
Controls: Adapt the real-world evaluation to various scenarios, such as different lighting conditions, screen sizes, or gaze intensity levels; simulate real-world variability in gaze data using techniques such as gaze-sampling or gaze-synthetic generation; validate that the model's adaptation capacity is linked to the quality of the fusion mechanism.
Estimated cost: 40 GPU-hours ( adds the cost for the real-world simulation)
Prediction: Expected results demonstrate ViLT-B32-Gaze's robustness in real-world scenarios, and the benefits and limitations of the fusion strategy under real-world conditions;  a concentration on the hardware, software or platform may prove effective or countering that appear when analyzing results simply.

PROPOSAL 6: Evaluating the Long-Term Effectiveness of Gaze-Guided Visual Token Construction in Egocentric User Intent Understanding
Conduct a long-term study to assess ViLT-B32-Gaze's performance on egocentric user intent understanding over a prolonged period of training and fine-tuning; monitor the model's adaptability to changing user behaviors, environmental conditions, and new task distributions.
Controls: Set up a continuous training and evaluation framework for ViLT-B32-Gaze, utilizing active learning or streaming data to introduce new and challenging examples; evaluate the model's ability to generalize to unseen tasks, users, or environments; compare long-term performance with a gaze-free baseline model.
Estimated cost: 50 GPU-hours (significantly increased over previous proposals)
Prediction: Expected results provide insights into ViLT-B32-Gaze's long-term adaptability and effectiveness; demonstrate its ability to learn from and adapt to changing user behaviors and task distributions.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Egocentric MLLMs with Gaze Cues
PROPOSAL: Experimentally compare the performance of existing MLLMs (e.g. LLaMA, PaLM) on the EPIC-Kitchens and Ego4D egocentric video question answering benchmarks with and without gaze information. Specifically, use gaze-centric tokenization and attention mechanisms to represent gaze signals and study their impact on user intent understanding.
CONTROLS: Evaluate MLLMs with (1) no gaze information, (2) gaze-centric tokenization (ablation), (3) gaze-centric attention (ablation), and (4) both gaze-centric tokenization and attention.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show significant improvements in understanding user intent from egocentric videos when gaze information is incorporated, but the extent of improvement might vary depending on the model architecture and gaze accuracy. Potential failure point: issues in gaze estimation and tracking might lead to inaccurate gaze signals, hindering the model's ability to utilize gaze cues.

This proposal will set a baseline for understanding the potential benefits of gaze information in egocentric video question answering and provides a clear starting point for further research on integrating gaze cues with MLLMs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze-Aware LLMs for Egocentric Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Develop a gaze-aware MLLM variant (e.g., GazeGPT) that incorporates gaze-centric tokenization and attention mechanisms into the model architecture. Train the model on the EPIC-Kitchens and Ego4D datasets with gaze information, and evaluate its performance on egocentric video question answering tasks.
CONTROLS: (1) GazeGPT with gaze-centric tokenization, (2) GazeGPT with gaze-centric attention, (3) GazeGPT with both gaze-centric tokenization and attention, (4) baseline MLLM (e.g., LLaMA).
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the gaze-aware MLLM variant, GazeGPT, outperforms the baseline MLLM on egocentric video question answering tasks, particularly in cases where the question is conditioned on user attention. Potential failure point: the improved performance might be limited to specific gaze tracking quality or gaze-centric features, which could undermine the model's generalizability.

This proposal aims to push the development of MLLMs further towards proactive personal AI assistants by enabling them to understand user intent more accurately.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Gaze-Aware LLMs for Egocentric Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: REVISITED PROPOSAL.
Incorporate a gaze-controlled knowledge navigator into GazeGPT, which allows the model to selectively focus on specific parts of the scene or specific event in the video when answering questions that require visual reasoning or user intent understanding. Implement the navigator as a sequence of gaze-centric attention modules that reweight the input tokens based on their relevance to the question and user attention.
CONTROLS: (1) GazeGPT with gaze-controlled knowledge navigator, (2) GazeGPT without navigator, (3) baseline MLLM (e.g., LLaMA), (4) GazeGPT with navigator but without additional gaze training data.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours (added 1000 GPU-hours for Gaze-controlled knowledge navigator)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the gaze-controlled knowledge navigator significantly enhances GazeGPT's performance on egocentric video question answering tasks, especially in cases where the question requires understanding specific events or activities. Potential failure point: the navigator might be overly sensitive to abrupt gaze movements or context switching, leading to decreased performance.

This revised proposal aims to further enhance the capabilities of MLLMs in understanding user intent from egocentric videos by enabling them to selectively focus on visually relevant parts of the scene or event.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancing Gaze-Aware MLLMs with Egocentric Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: 2. REVISED PROPOSAL.
Merge the gaze-aware MLLM variant (GazeGPT) developed in proposal 2 with recent advances in egocentric scene understanding, specifically object and scene graph-based reasoning. This revised model will be able to not only better understand user intent from gaze signals but also more effectively utilize egocentric scene context to answer questions. Integrate an object detection module and a scene graph construction module into GazeGPT, allowing it to better recognize objects and their relationships in the scene.
CONTROLS: (1) GazeGPT with object detection and scene graph construction, (2) GazeGPT without object and scene graph module, (3) baseline MLLM (e.g., LLaMA), (4) GazeGPT with gaze-controlled knowledge navigator from proposal 3.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours (added 500 GPU-hours for object detection and scene graph construction)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the revised GazeGPT outperforms the baseline MLLM and the original GazeGPT on egocentric video question answering tasks, by effectively combining gaze-awareness with scene understanding capabilities. Potential failure point: the increased complexity of the model might lead to overfitting, requiring careful tuning of the hyperparameters.

This revised proposal aims to complement the benefits of gaze-awareness with the strength of egocentric scene understanding to develop more capable proactive personal AI assistants.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Egocentric MLLMs with Gaze Cues
PROPOSAL: 1. REVISED PROPOSAL.
Modify the experiment to include gaze accuracy as a factor, with gaze estimates generated from various state-of-the-art eye-tracking algorithms. Investigate how different gaze accuracy levels impact the performance of MLLMs on egocentric video question answering tasks. Use the same ablation Study of controls 1, 2, 3 and 4, but now with varying degrees of gaze accuracy.
CONTROLS: (1) Gaze estimates with 95% accuracy, (2) Gaze estimates with 80% accuracy, (3) Gaze estimates with 60% accuracy, (4) baseline MLLM (e.g., LLaMA), (5) baseline MLLM with gaze information but without any gaze cues present.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours (no change)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that gaze accuracy significantly affects the performance of MLLMs on egocentric video question answering tasks, with higher accuracy leading to better results. Potential failure point: if the gaze accuracy is too low, the model might not be able to effectively utilize gaze cues, despite having them available.

This revised proposal aims to provide more insights into the relationship between gaze accuracy and egocentric MLLM performance, which is crucial for practical applications of gaze-aware proactive personal AI assistants.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Gaze-Aware MLLMs on User Preference
PROPOSAL: Develop a user study to evaluate the user experience of proactive personal AI assistants that utilize gaze-aware MLLMs. Design a user interface that leverages the gaze-aware MLLM to provide personalized recommendations and answers to users' questions. Measure user preference, engagement, and salvation by comparing the gaze-aware MLLM to a baseline LLM-based interface.
CONTROLS: (1) Gaze-aware MLLM-based interface, (2) Baseline LLM-based interface, (3) Baseline LLM-based interface without gaze information (to assess the value of gaze-awareness in user experience).
COST: 800 GPU-hours (non-GPU compute resources used for user study)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that users prefer interfaces that utilize gaze-aware MLLMs, as they feel more in control and provided with more value, leading to increased user engagement and satisfaction. Potential failure point: the perceived benefits of gaze-awareness might be subjective and not consistently noticed by all users, affecting the study's outcomes.

This proposal focuses on the practical applications of gaze-aware proactive personal AI assistants and aims to demonstrate their value in human-AI interaction.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Gaze-Aware MLLMs on User Preference
PROPOSAL: 3. REVISED PROPOSAL.
Incorporate a gaze-based personalized summarization component into the user interface, which focuses on presenting information that is relevant to the user's current attention and interests based on their gaze signals. Evaluate how users interact with and respond to the information presented, and measure the impact on their productivity and workload. Compare the performance of the gaze-aware MLLM-based interface with the baseline LLM-based interface and a gaze-based attention-aware interface.
CONTROLS: (1) Gaze-aware MLLM-based interface with gaze-based summarization, (2) Baseline LLM-based interface without gaze information, (3) Gaze-based attention-aware interface without MLLM capabilities.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (no additional increase due to non-GPU dependencies added)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the gaze-aware MLLM-based interface with gaze-based summarization component leads to significant productivity improvements and reduced workload for users, compared to the baseline and other interfaces. Potential failure point: issues with summarization quality or model inference might detract from the user experience, compromising the benefits of gaze-awareness.

This revised proposal extends the original user study and focuses on the practical applications of gaze-aware proactive personal AI assistants in optimizing user productivity and experience.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Robustness of Gaze-Aware MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of GazeGPT, the gaze-aware MLLM variant developed in proposal 2, against common MLLM perturbations (e.g., adversarial attacks, intentional noise injection) and gaze estimation errors. Evaluate GazeGPT's performance under various scenarios, including gaze signal degradation, low-quality gaze tracking, and manipulation of gaze information.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline GazeGPT, (2) GazeGPT with random gaze noise addition, (3) GazeGPT with adversarial gaze attacks, (4) GazeGPT with occlusion of gaze signals, (5) Baseline LLM without gaze-aware capabilities.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that GazeGPT is robust to various perturbations and errors, and maintains its performance advantage over the baseline LLM. However, potential failure points include: GazeGPT being vulnerable to advanced adversarial attacks or gaze signal manipulations, which could compromise its ability to interpret gaze cues accurately.

This proposal will contribute to understanding the limitations of gaze-aware MLLMs and provide insights into how to improve their robustness and reliability in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Developing a Benchmark for Egocentric Gaze-Aware MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Establish a new benchmark, EGaze, specifically designed to evaluate the performance of gaze-aware MLLMs on egocentric video question answering tasks. EGaze will comprise a dataset with diverse egocentric video scenarios, accurate gaze estimations, and challenging question answering tasks that require understanding user intent and gaze-aware reasoning. Develop a set of metrics to assess the capability of gaze-aware MLLMs in addressing user intent from egocentric videos with varying gaze accuracy levels.
CONTROLS: (1) EGaze benchmark with gaze-centric questions, (2) EGaze benchmark without gaze-centric questions, (3) Baseline LLM-based evaluation, (4) Comparison with other established benchmarks (e.g., EPIC-Kitchens, Ego4D).
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the EGaze benchmark effectively evaluates the capabilities of gaze-aware MLLMs and identifies areas for improvement, leading to better understanding and development of egocentric gaze-aware AI assistants. Potential failure point: the EGaze benchmark might require significant computational resources, making it challenging to release and maintain as an open-source benchmark.

This proposal aims to facilitate the development of gaze-aware MLLMs by providing a standardized benchmark, EGaze, and promoting the creation of more accurate and robust egocentric AI assistants.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Deployment and Validation of Gaze-Aware MLLMs in Real-World Applications
PROPOSAL: Collaborate with industry partners to deploy and validate the gaze-aware MLLMs developed in this research in real-world applications, such as smart home assistants, virtual concierges, and wheelchair navigation systems. Evaluate the practical benefits of gaze-awareness and assess its impact on user experience, productivity, and safety.
CONTROLS: (1) Real-world deployment of GazeGPT, (2) Baseline LLM-based deployment, (3) User study with real-world participants.
COST: Not estimated (partner-dependent)
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the deployment of gaze-aware MLLMs leads to significant improvements in user experience, productivity, and safety in various real-world applications. Potential failure point: issues with model deployment, training, and validation might affect the results and highlight the need for further improvements.

This proposal aims to bridge the gap between the lab-based experiments and real-world applications, demonstrating the practical value and potential of gaze-aware MLLMs in various industries and contexts.

Potential failure point: the perceived benefits of gaze-awareness might be subjective and not consistently noticed by all users, affecting the study's outcomes.

This proposal focuses on the practical applications of gaze-aware proactive personal AI assistants and aims to demonstrate their value in human-AI interaction.
propositions.texte: Develop a user study to evaluate the user experience of proactive personal AI assistants that utilize gaze-aware MLLMs. Design a user interface that leverages the gaze-aware MLLM to provide personalized recommendations and answers to users' questions. Measure user preference, engagement, and salvation by comparing the gaze-aware MLLM to a baseline LLM-based interface.
propositions.titre: Evaluating Gaze-Aware MLLMs on User Preference

propositions.controles: (1) Baseline GazeGPT, (2) GazeGPT with random gaze noise addition, (3) GazeGPT with adversarial gaze attacks, (4) GazeGPT with occlusion of gaze signals, (5) Baseline LLM without gaze-aware capabilities.
propositions.prediction:
Expected results show that GazeGPT is robust to various perturbations and errors, and maintains its performance advantage over the baseline LLM. However, potential failure points include: GazeGPT being vulnerable to advanced adversarial attacks or gaze signal manipulations, which could compromise its ability to interpret gaze cues accurately.

This proposal will contribute to understanding the limitations of gaze-aware MLLMs and provide insights into how to improve their robustness and reliability in real-world applications.
propositions.texte: Investigate the robustness of GazeGPT, the gaze-aware MLLM variant developed in proposal 2, against common MLLM perturbations (e.g., adversarial attacks, intentional noise injection) and gaze estimation errors. Evaluate GazeGPT's performance under various scenarios, including gaze signal degradation, low-quality gaze tracking, and manipulation of gaze information.
propositions.titre: Analyzing the Robustness of Gaze-Aware MLLMs

propositions.controles: (1) EGaze benchmark with gaze-centric questions, (2) EGaze benchmark without gaze-centric questions, (3) Baseline LLM-based evaluation, (4) Comparison with other established benchmarks (e.g., EPIC-Kitchens, Ego4D).
propositions.prediction:
Expected results show that the EGaze benchmark effectively evaluates the capabilities of gaze-aware MLLMs and identifies areas for improvement, leading to better understanding and development of egocentric gaze-aware AI assistants. Potential failure point: the EGaze benchmark might require significant computational resources, making it challenging to release and maintain as an open-source benchmark.

This proposal aims to facilitate the development of gaze-aware MLLMs by providing a standardized benchmark, EGaze, and promoting the creation of more accurate and robust egocentric AI assistants.
propositions.texte: Establish a new benchmark, EGaze, specifically designed to evaluate the performance of gaze-aware MLLMs on egocentric video question answering tasks. EGaze will comprise a dataset with diverse egocentric video scenarios, accurate gaze estimations, and challenging question answering tasks that require understanding user intent and gaze-aware reasoning. Develop a set of metrics to assess the capability of gaze-aware MLLMs in addressing user intent from egocentric videos with varying gaze accuracy levels.
propositions.titre: Developing a Benchmark for Egocentric Gaze-Aware MLLMs

propositions.controles: (1) Real-world deployment of GazeGPT, (2) Baseline LLM-based deployment, (3) User study with real-world participants.
propositions.prediction:
Expected results show that the deployment of gaze-aware MLLMs leads to significant improvements in user experience, productivity, and safety in various real-world applications. Potential failure point: issues with model deployment, training, and validation might affect the results and highlight the need for further improvements.

This proposal aims to bridge the gap between the lab-based experiments and real-world applications, demonstrating the practical value and potential of gaze-aware MLLMs in various industries and contexts.
propositions.texte: Collaborate with industry partners to deploy and validate the gaze-aware MLLMs developed in this research in real-world applications, such as smart home assistants, virtual concierges, and wheelchair navigation systems. Evaluate the practical benefits of gaze-awareness and assess its impact on user experience, productivity, and safety.
propositions.titre: Deployment and Validation of Gaze-Aware MLLMs in Real-World Applications

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark Development for Egocentric Video Question Answering with Gaze Cues
PROPOSAL: Develop a new egocentric video question answering benchmark, EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE, which integrates user gaze information as an additional input modalitiy. EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE will include a diverse set of video clips from various egocentric scenarios (e.g., cooking, shopping, outdoor activities) with corresponding gaze data, question-answer pairs, and a moderating system to ensure data quality and balance.
CONTROLS: Evaluate against the existing egocentric video question answering benchmark (e.g.,GazeGPT) without gaze information to assess the effect of including gaze cues.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed benchmark will demonstrate the benefits of incorporating gaze information in improving MLLMs' understanding of user intent. Expected result: ±5% improvement in accuracy on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE compared to ego-centric VQA without gaze. Potential point of failure: the benchmark's over-reliance on a specific gaze tracking system could affect the generalizability of results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Gaze-MLLMs with CLIP and ViLT Architectures
PROPOSAL: Experiment with pre-trained CLIP and ViLT architectures which are known for their multimodal capabilities, to examine how they perform on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE and existing egocentric video question answering benchmarks without gaze information. Evaluate the performance of CLIP-ViT and ViLT-ViT models in capturing gaze-based user intent and compare their results on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE to those of existing multimodal models.
CONTROLS: Include Visual Transformer (ViT) as an baseline to compare the impact of CLIP and ViLT architectures on MLLMs' performance with gaze information.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Gaze-MLLMs with CLIP and ViLT Architectures
REVISED PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to include a comparison of different gaze input modalities and representations, such as gaze coordinates, gaze maps, and gaze heatmaps, on the performance of CLIP and ViLT-based MLLMs on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE. Explore using state-of-the-art gaze estimation models to generate gaze data for datasets without explicit gaze annotations.
CONTROLS: Include experiments with different gaze processing approaches (e.g., using raw gaze coordinates, binarizing gaze heatmaps) and baseline studies on how MLLMs perform when given different types of gaze data.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: The choice of gaze input modality significantly impacts MLLMs' performance on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE, with gaze heatmaps being the most informative input type. Models that receive gaze data directly during pre-training may outperform those that only incorporate gaze during fine-tuning.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Investigating Gaze-MLLMs with CLIP and ViLT Architectures
REVISED PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to compare the impact of incorporating gaze information in different stages of the CLIP and ViLT architectures, including pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference time. Investigate whether gaze-augmented pre-training improves model performance, whether gaze-informed fine-tuning adapts the model to the EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE task, or whether gaze-based attention mechanisms enhance inference accuracy.
CONTROLS: Include baseline studies on models without gaze information to understand the contribution of each integration strategy. Analyze which gaze-augmentation strategies provide the most benefits and in which scenarios (e.g., question type, gaze noise).
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: Gaze-augmented pre-training shows the most substantial benefits, but combining gaze-informed fine-tuning and gaze-based attention mechanisms during inference may yield the highest performance gains. However, the importance of each strategy might depend on the level of gaze noise and interference.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effectiveness of Different Eye-Tracking Methods for Gaze-Based Egocentric Video Understanding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of different eye-tracking methods (e.g., manual annotation, simulated gaze data, low-cost gaze-tracking devices) on the performance of gaze-enabled multimodal models on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE. Evaluate whether the accuracy and robustness of gaze-based systems depend on the quality and reliability of the eye-tracking data.
CONTROLS: Include comparisons with controllers that never include or may only happen once for any particular evaluation criteria, to understand how gaze methods impact overall MLLMs' performance and how much model performance varies with the eye-tracking noise.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: Models with high-quality, noise-free gaze data perform significantly better than those relying on simulated or lower-quality data. However, the threshold for model performance degradation might be lower for models fine-tuned with gaze data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding Gaze-MLLMs Failure Modes in Egocentric Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Investigate the failure modes of CLIP and ViLT-based models trained with gaze information on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE, focusing on cases where explicit gaze data contradicts the visual context or when models fail to attend to crucial regions of interest. Analyze the types of questions and clips that are most challenging for gaze-MLLMs to answer correctly.
CONTROLS: Conduct a thorough error analysis to identify where and which types of gaze integration lead to errors in the models and provide open er examples for the examiners selection or approving.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: Gaze-MLLMs tend to fail in scenarios with complex gaze relationships, low-gaze-quality data, and multimodal misalignment between visual and gaze inputs. However, scrutinizing the results will reveal a tight interplay between data quality, question complexity, and the accuracy of each model.

Compare this approach to existing gaze-augmentation strategies, such as gaze-based attention mechanisms or gaze-informed fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Include experiments with a wide variety of datasets, both previously used, and synthetic ones specifically developing that the multiple task-sharing schemes that such vlog may entail.
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: Gaze-supervised pre-training yields the best results for models integrating gaze information, providing accurate representations of user intent and gaze. However, significantly dependencies will invariably be present just like how delayed ae ok in multiheads.

TITLE: Prospective Study of Multimodal Personal AI Assistants Leveraging Egocentric Video and Gaze Data
PROPOSAL: Conduct a prospective study to investigate the deployment of gaze-MLLMs in real-world, proactive personal AI assistants and evaluate their feasibility, usefulness, and user acceptance in various everyday scenarios, such as indoor navigation, virtual meetings, or shopping. Record user interactions, self-reported feedback, and system performance metrics.

PREDICTION: Expected result: Gaze-MLLMs-powered personal AI assistants will lead to improved user experiences and increased user trust due to enhanced context understanding.

TITLE: Implicit Gaze Embeddings for Egocentric Video Understanding
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel approach to incorporating gaze information in MLLMs by learning implicit gaze embeddings that capture gaze patterns and relationships within egocentric videos. Investigate how implicit gaze embeddings enhance model performance on EGOCENTRIC-VQA-GAZE and how they compare to explicit gaze-based models.

COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: Implicit gaze embeddings will demonstrate competitive performance to explicit gaze-based models, offering a more interpretable and flexible approach to leveraging gaze information in MLLMs. However, ensuring accurate gaze data will remain a significant challenge.

TITLE: Towards a Unified Framework for Egocentric Video Understanding with Gaze
PROPOSAL: Synthesize the principles and findings from the previous experiments to develop a unified framework for incorporating gaze information in MLLMs for egocentric video understanding. The framework should provide a holistic solution for handling gaze, eye-tracking methods, and multimodal model architectures to ensure efficient, accurate, and scalable egocentric video understanding.
